owner_reason: Label reads MISSONI UOMO, MADE IN ITALY. Only 'Mizone' was the mishearing - the ledger had 'Uomo' right. Claude first read it as Missoni Sport off a small tile; the owner corrected it and the full-resolution label confirms Uomo.
lesson: A misheard brand can hide a collected name. And a line name read off a thumbnail is not read at all - Missoni Uomo and Missoni Sport are different lines with different values, so the tile has to be opened at full size before either is written down.

owner_reason: Label reads Fay. 'Fur' was the voice note's rendering of 'Fay'.
lesson: The ledger's fur warning and its platform-restriction worry both fall away. A misheard brand can also invent a compliance problem that does not exist.

owner_reason: Owner: neck label cut out so only worth 19.99.
lesson: A cut-out neck label is a pricing fault, not a footnote. It takes an Izod Lacoste knit BELOW the 20 floor for poorer pieces, even when the garment is otherwise Very Good with no wear. The ledger recorded it as 'no inside label' under Colour/Description with Defects left as None, so it never reached the price - read 'no label' as a deduction and as something the buyer must be told, at the end of the Item Description like any other defect.

product: Barbour Beaufort wax jacket, made in England
owner_reason: Owner: the Barbour Beaufort was 99, not 119.
lesson: Second time the same mistake: a comp range was read from its middle-to-top instead of its mass. Made-in-England Beauforts do reach 160, but the bulk sell near 90-110, and this one is Good rather than Very Good with the wax worn - condition should have pulled it to the bottom of the band, not the middle. When a range is wide, price off the comps that match the CONDITION, not the average of the range.

product: Emanuel Ungaro Sport d'Hiver puffer jacket
owner_reason: Owner: 85 on the Emanuel Ungaro. Given as training, not as a re-upload.
lesson: The owner's OWN ledger price can be under-set, so 'the ledger price wins' is not the end of the thought. Claude saw the comp band at 60-110, put 69.99 at its quick-sale end and said nothing. New rule: keep the dictated price, but SAY SO when it sits near the bottom of the band. Also the directional pattern - corrections on designer and collectable names go UP (Burberry 89.99 to 150, Ungaro 69.99 to 85) while corrections on volume vintage go DOWN (Izod 32.99 to 19.99, Beaufort 119.99 to 99.99). Rarity is being under-weighted and comp volume over-weighted.
